pages.headline: India and EU conclude FTA talks
pages.what: India and the European Union announced the conclusion of FTA negotiations at the 16th India-EU Summit in New Delhi, covering a market of about 2 billion people. The deal still needs legal scrubbing and ratification. An EU-India Security and Defence Partnership was also signed.
key: Concluded 27 January 2026, New Delhi; zone of about 2 billion people
EU is India's 22nd FTA partner
Talks began 2007, suspended 2013, relaunched 2022
No EU concessions on sugar, ethanol, rice, soft wheat, beef, poultry, milk powders, bananas, honey
Security and Defence Partnership signed: EU's third in Asia after Japan and South Korea
pages.static: Free trade agreements vs Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreements; WTO rules.
pages.angle: Assuming conclusion of talks means the deal is already in force.
pages.remember: Concluded, not yet ratified: 22nd FTA partner.

pages.headline: Merz visits India
pages.what: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz made his first visit to India as Chancellor, holding talks with Prime Minister Modi at Mahatma Mandir, Gandhinagar. Outcomes included a roadmap on defence co-development and visa-free transit through German airports for Indian passport holders.
key: First visit as Chancellor; talks at Mahatma Mandir, Gandhinagar
25 years of strategic partnership; 75 years of diplomatic relations
Roadmap on defence co-development and co-production
Visa-free transit through German airports for Indian passport holders
Germany to join MILAN, IONS and Tarang Shakti; backs IMEC
pages.static: Strategic partnerships; Indian Ocean Naval Symposium; IMEC.
pages.angle: Imagining Germany joining the Quad.
pages.remember: Merz in Gujarat: MILAN, IONS, Tarang Shakti, not Quad.

pages.headline: UAE President visits New Delhi
pages.what: UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan made an official visit to New Delhi. India and the UAE signed a Letter of Intent toward a Strategic Defence Partnership and a 10-year LNG supply deal between HPCL and ADNOC Gas starting in 2028.
key: Letter of Intent: Strategic Defence Partnership
LNG deal: HPCL and ADNOC Gas, 10 years from 2028, 0.5 million tonnes a year
Trade target: USD 100 billion to USD 200 billion by 2032

Explore SMRs, a 'House of India' in Abu Dhabi, 'Digital Embassies'
pages.static: India-UAE CEPA, 2022; energy diplomacy.
pages.angle: Naming IOC instead of HPCL as the LNG buyer.
pages.remember: HPCL buys UAE gas from 2028.

pages.headline: India's FTA network: Oman, NZ and the RCEP gap
pages.what: After concluding talks with New Zealand, India has FTAs with all RCEP members except China. Recent deals include the Oman CEPA, UK CETA and EFTA TEPA. The EU deal followed in January 2026.

India-Oman CEPA signed December 2025

India-EFTA TEPA signed March 2024

pages.angle: Mixing up signing and entry-into-force years.
pages.remember: Oman Dec 25, UK Jul 25, EFTA Mar 24.

pages.headline: Adani begins Wangchhu hydro project in Bhutan
pages.what: Adani Group started construction of the 570 MW Wangchhu Hydroelectric Project, a run-of-river scheme on the Wangchu (Raidak) river in Chukha District, Bhutan. The joint venture is Adani Power (49%) and Druk Green Power Corporation (51%), investing about Rs 6,000 crore.
key: 570 MW run-of-river project, Wangchu (Raidak) river, Chukha district
Joint venture: Adani Power 49%, Druk Green Power 51%
Build-own-operate-transfer basis
Investment about Rs 6,000 crore
Winter power for Bhutan; summer surplus exported to India
pages.static: India-Bhutan hydropower cooperation; run-of-river vs storage projects.
pages.angle: Reversing the equity split or calling it a storage project.
pages.remember: Bhutan holds 51; Adani holds 49.

pages.headline: India rejects China's Shaksgam activity
pages.what: India rejected Chinese infrastructure activity in the Shaksgam Valley as illegal and invalid after China asserted the area is Chinese territory. India reaffirmed that the valley is an integral part of India.
key: Shaksgam Valley (Trans-Karakoram Tract) lies north of Siachen Glacier

pages.static: Geography of Ladakh and Karakoram; India-China boundary questions.
pages.angle: Confusing Shaksgam with Aksai Chin.
pages.remember: Shaksgam: north of Siachen; ceded 1963.

pages.headline: India chairs BRICS 2026
pages.what: India holds the BRICS chairship for 2026 and will host the summit in New Delhi. The UAE backed the chairmanship in the India-UAE joint statement of 19 January 2026, and the RBI proposed putting BRICS CBDC linkage on the agenda.
key: India chairs BRICS in 2026; summit in New Delhi
Chairship rotates annually

pages.angle: Placing the 2025 declaration in the wrong city.
pages.remember: India chairs BRICS 2026; CBDCs on agenda.

pages.headline: Spain joins IPOI
pages.what: India welcomed Spain joining the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative, a voluntary non-treaty arrangement launched by India in November 2019 at the East Asia Summit in Bangkok. 2026 is the India-Spain Dual Year of Culture, Tourism and AI.
key: IPOI launched Nov 2019, East Asia Summit, Bangkok; non-treaty

pages.remember: Seven pillars; Australia and Thailand lead ecology.

pages.headline: India signs the Pax Silica Declaration
pages.what: India joined the US-led Pax Silica initiative for trusted technology supply chains. It also signed a joint statement on an India-US AI Opportunity Partnership as an addendum.
key: US-led initiative for a secure technology ecosystem
Covers semiconductors, AI infrastructure, critical minerals, compute

pages.headline: India's first engagement with Weimar Triangle
pages.what: India's External Affairs Minister took part in India's first-ever engagement with the Weimar Triangle, along with French and Polish counterparts and German representatives. The grouping was formed in 1991 to anchor German-Polish reconciliation.

Formed 29 August 1991, joint declaration, Weimar, Germany

Poland joined NATO in 1999 and the EU in 2004
No institutional structure; India engaged, did not join

pages.angle: Treating the engagement as membership.

pages.headline: 2nd India-Arab Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Delhi
pages.what: India was set to host all 22 Arab League members for the 2nd India-Arab Foreign Ministers' Meeting. A new India-Arab Countries Chambers of Commerce, Industry and Agriculture was to be inaugurated.

pages.headline: US strikes Venezuela, captures Maduro
pages.what: United States forces struck Caracas and captured Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores, flown to New York for narco-terrorism charges. The operation was justified by a 'Trump Corollary' to the Monroe Doctrine. Venezuela's Supreme Court named Delcy Rodriguez interim president.

pages.angle: Giving the wrong US city for Maduro's arraignment.
pages.remember: Caracas strike; Maduro in New York.

pages.headline: US exits 66 bodies including ISA
pages.what: A US presidential memorandum signed around 7 January 2026 directed withdrawal from 66 international organisations, including 31 UN entities such as the IPCC and UN DESA, and the India-France-led International Solar Alliance.

pages.headline: Trump launches Board of Peace at Davos
pages.what: US President Donald Trump launched the 'Board of Peace' at Davos, where leaders signed its charter, with reports of about 35 signatory countries. India was invited but did not attend. It was set up for Gaza under UN Security Council Resolution 2803 (2025).

pages.headline: Trump announces Greenland 'framework'
pages.what: At Davos, US President Trump announced a 'framework of a future deal' on Greenland and dropped a threatened tariff on eight European countries. He said he would not use force to acquire Greenland.

pages.headline: Bulgaria joins the eurozone
pages.what: Bulgaria adopted the euro on 1 January 2026, replacing the lev, and became the 21st member of the eurozone. Croatia had joined in 2023 as the 20th member.

pages.headline: New UNSC non-permanent members
pages.what: Bahrain, Colombia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Latvia and Liberia began two-year terms as non-permanent members of the UN Security Council on 1 January 2026, running through 2027. They were elected by the General Assembly in June 2025.

pages.headline: High Seas Treaty enters into force
pages.what: The BBNJ Agreement entered into force on 17 January 2026, the first legally binding treaty for conserving marine biodiversity in international waters. It was adopted in 2023 under UNCLOS, 120 days after the 60th ratification took effect.

pages.headline: UK defends Chagos deal
pages.what: The United Kingdom defended its agreement to transfer the Chagos archipelago to Mauritius while retaining a 99-year lease on the Diego Garcia base, after criticism from US President Trump. The ICJ's 2019 advisory opinion had found the 1965 detachment unlawful.

99-year lease on Diego Garcia retained

pages.headline: DRDO completes Akash-NG user trials
pages.what: DRDO completed user evaluation trials of the Akash-NG surface-to-air missile with the Indian Air Force as the user. It has a range of up to 70 km, Mach 2.5 speed and about 96 per cent indigenous content.

pages.headline: 78th Army Day in Jaipur
pages.what: The 78th Army Day was observed in Jaipur, Rajasthan, the first Army Day parade held outside a cantonment. The new Bhairav Battalions made their debut and the Army named 2026 the 'Year of Networking and Data Centricity'.

pages.what: DRDO's Long Range Anti-Ship Hypersonic Missile was showcased for the first time at the 77th Republic Day parade. It is a hypersonic glide missile with a range of about 1,500 km, reaching up to Mach 10.

pages.what: DRDO test-fired two Pralay missiles and flight-tested the MPATGM against a moving target. The Army signed a Rs 293 crore deal for the Suryastra long-range rocket launcher.

pages.headline: NATGRID linked to NPR
pages.what: NATGRID was integrated with the National Population Register, giving authorised agencies access to family-level data of about 119 crore residents. The intelligence grid was conceived in 2009 after the 26/11 attacks.

pages.headline: INSV Kaundinya reaches Muscat
pages.what: INSV Kaundinya, India's first 'stitched ship' built with the ancient Tankai method, reached Port Sultan Qaboos in Muscat, Oman, from Porbandar on its maiden voyage. Eutelsat provided connectivity through its OneWeb constellation.
